transcript.text: My indesit washing machine fills with water and drains but the drum just doesn't go round at all. Its an IWC something. Had it about 9 years. Is it worth fixing?

For a 9-year-old Indesit that fills and drains but won't spin, the most likely cause is a broken or slipped drive belt. To confirm this safely, please unplug the appliance first. Then remove the two screws at the back of the top panel, slide the panel forward and lift it off. Look down into the drum area; if you can see a large pulley wheel with no belt around it (or a loose belt), that is your fault. Let me know what you see.

I've unplugged it and had a look at the belt. It's sitting on the pulleys and feels tight, so it doesn't look like the belt. I did notice a faint hot electrical smell a few weeks ago, though not since. What should I check next?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. This points strongly to an internal safety cut-out inside the motor—most likely a thermal fuse that has blown due to overheating. You will need to call an engineer to diagnose and replace the faulty component (usually the motor or its thermal fuse).

candidates: Drive belt broken or slipped off (high)
Motor brush wear or motor failure (medium)
Drum obstruction (e.g. lost coin under baffle) (low)
